messages:
maria: Quick sync — need to triage serving runtime changes for next quarter. Kernel selection heuristics + attention optimizations + KV cache eviction policy. Can we scope an RFC + short PRD by EoW next week? We need concrete launch criteria for Dedicated customers (AcmeSearch SLA), Hosted fallbacks, and an ops rollback plan.

eli: I can own the RFC draft. Main risks to call out: latency regressions on long-context traces and quality drift for quantized kernels. Proposal for acceptance criteria (draft): p50 <= baseline + 10ms, p95 <= baseline + 50ms, steady-state throughput >= 90% of baseline. Fallback to previous kernel variant if any abort condition is hit.

raj: Infra note — Dedicated fleets vary (A100 vs H100 mixes), so kernel selector needs to be topology-aware. Suggest adding a kernel preference score: stability, memory footprint, compute efficiency. Also require canary rollout at 5-10% traffic with node-level tagging. Ops needs a kill-switch that routes to the pinned model variant.

sophia: From ML/evals side, add a quality acceptance: run the canonical regression suite (1000 prompts) and require semantic-similarity delta <= 0.5% (emb-based), or <1% for edge cases. Also include a tiny synthetic stress test for attention patterns: long, nested, repeated tokens.

maria: Good call. For KV cache edge cases we need to enumerate: eviction on shard migration, TTL inconsistencies after rollbacks, cold-start hit-rate collapse. Acceptance: cache-hit-rate drop < 3% during rollout; no persistent correctness violations (missing KV entries for active sessions).

eli: Draft RFC outline I'll push:
- Motivation + customers (AcmeSearch, internal perf teams)
- Compat matrix (model precisions, sequence lengths)
- Kernel selection algorithm (scoring, heuristics, forced overrides)
- Attention opt details (fused kernels, block-sparse heuristics)
- KV policy (TTL, LRU variants, cross-shard sync)
- Benchmarks (latency/throughput/quality) and test harness
- Rollout plan, canary %, abort conditions, metrics
- Acceptance criteria and post-rollout monitoring

eli: Putting a minimal rollout config snippet here for the PRD/RF C: 
```yaml
kernel_rollout:
  strategy: canary
  percent: 10
  metrics:
    - name: p95_latency_ms
      max_increase: 50
    - name: semantic_regression_pct
      max: 0.5
  abort_on:
    - metric: p95_latency_ms
      threshold_increase: 50
    - metric: semantic_regression_pct
      threshold: 0.5
```

maria: Nice. Also add operational acceptance: deploy restores to pinned variant within 30s, alerting to #incidents and #eng-oncall with automated rollback. For Dedicated customers, include SLA note and opt-out window during migration.

raj: One more: quantify perf targets per gpu-class. I'll attach a small table in the RFC (A100 p50 baseline, H100 p50 baseline, etc.).

sophia: I'll prepare the regression prompt set and an automated eval notebook that runs in CI. We should gate canary promotion on both perf and eval pass.

deploy-bot: scheduled: RFC draft pushed to repo at 1795004380 by eli. Canary rollout window reserved: 48h.

maria: Ok assigning owners: eli -> RFC + rollout plan, raj -> infra rollout hooks + kill-switch, sophia -> eval suite, ops -> define alert runbook. Target: RFC + PRD draft by 1795600000 (next-week EoW). Ping if blockers. :thumbsup:
